- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply a 1–2% upward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment >0.5.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, add 0.5–1% to avoid missing rebound.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00) triggers downward bias correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days, then revert to baseline if sentiment recovers.
